related_questions.question: What percentage of the world has asthma?

text_blocks.snippet: Approximately 9.8% of the global population has experienced asthma at some point in their lives. In 2019, the global prevalence of current asthma, as diagnosed by a doctor, was estimated to be 5.4% among individuals aged 5-69. This translates to roughly 357.4 million people diagnosed with asthma. A larger number, 645.2 million people, have had asthma at some point in their lives.

list.title: Prevalence of current wheezing:
list.snippet: The highest prevalence of current wheezing among those aged 5-69 was in the African Region at 13.2%, while the lowest was in the Americas Region at 10.0%, according to the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

list.title: Prevalence of ever asthma:
list.snippet: The African Region also had the highest prevalence of "ever asthma" (11.3%), while South-East Asia had the lowest (8.8%).

list.title: Prevalence of doctor-diagnosed asthma:
list.snippet: Globally, about 4.3% of adults have a doctor's diagnosis of asthma, while 4.5% report having a doctor's diagnosis or are taking asthma medication.

list.title: Prevalence of asthma symptoms:
list.snippet: Around 8.6% of adults report experiencing wheezing or whistling breath in the past 12 months, according to the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

list.title: Regional differences:
list.snippet: Asthma prevalence varies significantly by region, with higher rates in developed countries and among disadvantaged populations in those countries.

list.title: Age variations:
list.snippet: Asthma is the most common chronic disease among children.

related_questions.question: What is the 4 4 4 rule for asthma?

text_blocks.snippet: The 4-4-4 rule in asthma first aid refers to a specific sequence of actions to take when someone is experiencing an asthma attack: 4 puffs of a reliever inhaler, 4 breaths after each puff, and waiting 4 minutes before repeating. If symptoms don't improve after the first cycle, repeat the process and then seek further medical help if needed.
snippet_highlighted_words: 4 puffs of a reliever inhaler, 4 breaths after each puff, and waiting 4 minutes before repeating

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a breakdown of the 4-4-4 rule:

list.title: 1. 4 puffs:
list.snippet: Use a blue or grey reliever inhaler (like Ventolin or Bricanyl) and administer one puff at a time.

list.title: 2. 4 breaths:
list.snippet: After each puff, take 4 breaths, ideally with a spacer if available, to ensure the medication reaches the lungs.

list.title: 3. Wait 4 minutes:
list.snippet: Allow the medication to take effect. If symptoms persist, repeat the 4 puffs and 4 breaths.

list.title: 4. Seek further help:
list.snippet: If the person's condition doesn't improve after the second cycle, call emergency services (e.g., 911 in the US, 000 in Australia) immediately.

list.title: 5. Continue administering:
list.snippet: Keep giving 4 puffs every 4 minutes until emergency help arrives.
Spacer: Using a spacer with the inhaler is recommended as it helps deliver the medication more effectively to the lungs.
Calmness: It's crucial to stay calm and reassure the person experiencing the attack.
Positioning: Have the person sit upright, as lying down can worsen breathing difficulties.
Clothing: Loosen any tight clothing around the neck and chest.
Asthma Action Plan: If the person has a written Asthma Action Plan, follow the instructions in the plan.

related_questions.title: Facts and Stats - 8.3% of Americans Have Asthma | ACAAI ...

text_blocks.snippet: In 2021, asthma affected an estimated 24.9 million people in the U.S., including 4.7 million children and 20.3 million adults, representing 7.7% of the population. Asthma prevalence varies across different demographics, with higher rates among certain racial and ethnic groups, and females. Poorly controlled asthma can significantly impact daily life, leading to missed school or work days and increased emergency room visits and hospitalizations.
snippet_highlighted_words: In 2021, asthma affected an estimated 24.9 million people in the U.S., including 4.7 million children and 20.3 million adults, representing 7.7% of the population

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed look at asthma statistics:

list.snippet: Overall: In 2021, 7.7% of the U.S. population had asthma, according to the CDC.
By Age: Asthma prevalence is higher in children aged 10-17 years (9.1%) compared to younger children (2.6%).
By Sex: Females are more likely to have asthma than males.
By Race/Ethnicity: Non-Hispanic Black adults and children have higher rates of asthma compared to non-Hispanic White individuals, according to the CDC.
By Family Income: Asthma prevalence tends to be higher among those with lower family incomes, according to the American Lung Association.

list.title: Missed Days:
list.snippet: Asthma can lead to missed school and work days due to symptoms or attacks.

list.title: Emergency Visits & Hospitalizations:
list.snippet: Asthma accounts for a significant number of emergency room visits and hospitalizations annually.

list.title: Economic Burden:
list.snippet: The economic cost of asthma is estimated to be billions of dollars annually.

list.title: Deaths:
list.snippet: While asthma death rates have decreased over time, asthma still contributes to a number of deaths each year.

list.title: Overall:
list.snippet: Asthma prevalence has generally increased since 1980, according to Mass.gov.

list.title: Children:
list.snippet: Asthma prevalence among children has decreased in recent years, according to the CDC.

list.title: Adults:
list.snippet: Asthma prevalence among adults has shown a non-significant decrease in some periods and a significant increase in others, according to the CDC.

list.title: Family History:
list.snippet: Individuals with a family history of asthma are more likely to develop the condition.

list.title: Allergies:
list.snippet: Asthma is more common in individuals with other allergic conditions, such as eczema and hay fever.

list.title: Environmental Factors:
list.snippet: Urban living and exposure to certain allergens and irritants can increase the risk of asthma.
